39.11% }} {{Elections in California}} Two '''2022 United States Senate elections in California''' were held concurrently on November 8, 2022, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[California]]. There were two ballot items for the same [[Classes of United States senators|Class 3 seat]]: a special election to fill the seat for the final weeks of the [[117th United States Congress]] (ending on January 3, 2023), and a general election for a full term (beginning on the same day), starting in the [[118th United States Congress]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Alex Padilla]] was appointed in 2021 by [[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] to fill the vacancy created by [[Kamala Harris]]'s election to the [[Vice President of the United States|vice presidency]] in [[2020 United States presidential election|2020]], and he sought a full term.{{Cite news|last=Wilson|first=Reid|date=September 28, 2021|title=California rule change means Padilla faces extra election|work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/574242-california-rule-change-means-padilla-faces-extra-election|url-status=live|access-date=September 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928225230/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/574242-california-rule-change-means-padilla-faces-extra-election|archive-date=September 28, 2021}}{{cite web|last1=Willon|first1=Phil|last2=McGreevy|first2=Patrick|url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-12-22/gavin-newsom-alex-padilla-senate-california-kamala-harris|title=Alex Padilla becomes California's first Latino U.S. senator, replacing Kamala Harris|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=December 22, 2020|access-date=December 22, 2020}} A [[nonpartisan primary]] for each of the terms took place on June 7.{{cite web|title=Statewide Direct Primary Election - June 7, 2022|url=https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/upcoming-elections/statewide-direct-primary-election-june-7-2022|url-status=live|access-date=September 28, 2021|website=[[California Secretary of State]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201223100223/https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/upcoming-elections/statewide-direct-primary-election-june-7-2022 |archive-date=December 23, 2020 }} The top two candidates in each primary, regardless of party, advanced to the special and regular general elections in November. With his advancement out of the primary, Mark P. Meuser ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɔɪ|ʒ|ər}} {{respell|MOY|zhər}}) became the first Republican since [[2012 United States Senate election in California|2012]] to advance to the general election, as both the [[2016 United States Senate election in California|2016]] and [[2018 United States Senate election in California|2018 Senate elections]] solely featured Democrats as the top two candidates. This race was a rematch between the two, as both had previously run for the secretary of state in [[2018 California Secretary of State election|2018]]. Padilla won both elections with more than 60% of the vote.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-09 |title=Alex Padilla makes history as first Latino elected to U.S. Senate from California |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2022-11-08/2022-california-midterm-election-padilla-first-latino-u-s-senate-california |access-date=2022-11-09 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}} He became the first [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latino]] elected to the U.S. Senate from California, and the first male elected to the Senate from California since [[Pete Wilson]] was re-elected in [[1988 United States Senate election in California|1988]] and the first male elected to the Class 3 Senate seat from California since [[Alan Cranston]] was re-elected in [[1986 United States Senate election in California|1986]].{{cite web | url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/08/politics/2022-midterm-election-historic-firsts/index.html | title=Meet the history-makers of the 2022 midterm elections | CNN Politics | website=[[CNN]] | date=November 9, 2022 }} This was the first time since [[1988 United States Senate election in California|1988]] that both major party final candidates for a Senate seat in California were men and was also the first time that both major party candidates for the Class 3 Senate seat in California were men since [[1986 United States Senate election in California|1986]]. ==Candidates== ===Democratic Party=== ====Advanced to general==== *[[Alex Padilla]], incumbent U.S. senator (2021–present) and former [[Secretary of State of California|secretary of state of California]] (2015–2021){{Cite news |date=December 23, 2020 |title=Alex Padilla and Shirley Weber will run in 2022. Padilla's election strategy focused on advocating for [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] policies and building ties with left-wing organizations that had a poor relationship with California's other Senator, [[Dianne Feinstein]].{{cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/Progressives-fed-up-with-Feinstein-want-her-to-16253415.php|title=Progressives fed up with Feinstein, want her to resign now|website=San Francisco Chronicle|last1=Garofoli|first1=Joe|date=June 16, 2021|accessdate=August 10, 2021}} The potential Democratic opponent to Padilla considered most likely to join the race was U.S. Representative [[Ro Khanna]], a staunchly left-wing Democrat who rose to prominence as the co-chair of the [[Bernie Sanders 2020 presidential campaign]], and who had a loyal base of support from California's [[Asian-American]] and [[Pacific Islander]] communities. On August 9, 2021, Khanna announced that he would be endorsing Padilla for election, which was viewed as likely ending any possibility that Padilla would face a serious Democratic opponent.{{cite news|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/Khanna-considered-challenging-Padilla-but-now-16373144.php|title=Khanna considered challenging Padilla, but now he's endorsing him for Senate|website=San Francisco Chronicle|last1=Garofoli|first1=Joe|date=August 9, 2021|accessdate=August 9, 2021}} It was noted by the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' that it was considered unlikely that Padilla would face any serious Republican opponent, as California's heavily Democratic lean caused potentially strong candidates, such as U.S. Representatives [[Mike Garcia (politician)|Mike Garcia]] and [[Young Kim]], to prefer to remain in their positions rather than launch a long-shot Senate run.{{cite news|last=Wildermuth|first=John|date=December 19, 2020|title=Can California GOP find a Senate candidate in 2022? If not, Alex Padilla could be set for years|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/Can-California-GOP-find-a-Senate-candidate-in-15832834.php|access-date=February 8, 2021|website=San Francisco Chronicle}} In April 2022, billionaire businessman Dan O'Dowd entered the race, launching a $650,000 ad campaign.
